Subject: RE: Ceres3b 503s from 08/01: immediate update and mitigation

Hi Aisha — thanks for the report and the sample files. Quick update from our side:

What we found so far:
- Our ops telemetry shows a correlated increase in KV-cache eviction rates for ceres3b-v2q workers starting 08:50 UTC. Evictions coincide with the rollout of a quantized kernel (v2q-2028-07-31) to a subset of the fleet.
- The new kernel reduces memory use generally but has an edge-case where long-context traffic triggers more frequent KV checkpointing, producing contention on the worker and elevated 95/99 tail latency. At scale that produced transient failures surfaced as 503s.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:55–09:05 UTC):
- Rolled back kernel v2q-2028-07-31 on the affected pool.
- Temporarily increased per-deployment min replicas for ceres3b-v2q to reduce cache churn.
- Enabled an emergency autoscale rule to allow faster warmup for long-context requests.

Result: By 09:35 UTC error rate dropped to <1% for observed traffic patterns. We're still monitoring; ops dump attached.

Next steps (24h plan):
- Karthik and Ben will run a targeted stress test to reproduce the edge-case and capture kernel-level traces (JIRA INFR-4529).
- We'll provide a patched kernel that preserves the memory wins but avoids the checkpoint frequency regression.
- We'll share a short mitigation guide for you (pin to ceres3b-v2a or enable smaller max-context until patch is available).

We appreciate the quick heads-up — I will keep you posted and will share the RCA once the postmortem is complete.

Attachments: ops-dump-ceres3b-0801.tar.gz

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps for Ceres3b 503s (INFR-4529)

Hi Aisha and team,

Thanks again for the report and patience while we investigated. This is a brief post-incident update covering root cause, what we changed, and our commitments. We also attached a one-page RCA PDF.

Root cause (summary):
- A rollout of a quantized kernel (v2q-2028-07-31) to a subset of ceres3b workers introduced an unintended change in KV checkpoint behavior for long-context sessions.
- For high-concurrency long-context workloads this increased cache churn and worker CPU contention, raising tail latency and causing transient 503s when workers could not reply within the gateway SLO.

What we did (already implemented):
- Immediate rollback of v2q-2028-07-31 to previous kernel across all affected pools (completed 08:55–09:05 UTC, Aug 1).
- Raised minimum replicas and tightened autoscale warmup to reduce cache churn for long-context deployments.
- Added an emergency fallback rule to route long-context traffic to a compatibility pool when tail latency > 500ms.

Short-term commitments (next 7 days):
- Provide a patched kernel candidate (v2q-2028-08-04-rc1) that addresses checkpoint frequency. We will run joint verification with your team before re-rollout.
- Share a recommended configuration for PureAnalytics: pin to ceres3b-v2a for highest stability or set max-context to 4k until verified.

Long-term fixes (30–90 days):
- Kernel integration tests will include long-context synthetic workloads for regression detection.
- Improve rollout canary rules to measure KV checkpoint metrics and automatic rollback thresholds.
- Documentation updates for customers on best practices for long-context deployments.

What we need from you:
- If possible, provide a short reproducible test plan (or traffic replay) so our infra team can validate the patched kernel in your environment.
- Confirm whether PureAnalytics wants Redwood to schedule a joint verification run on Aug 6–8.

Links: JIRA INFR-4529 (detailed traces and patch), drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/PA-CERES3B-0801

Attachments: rca-summary-pureanalytics-0803.pdf

We appreciate your partnership on this. Please reach out directly to me or @support if you have any questions or want to schedule the verification run.

Regards,
